notes.decision: Translated 'gate of the going-forth of the souls.' ⲡⲣⲟ here = ⲣⲟ 'mouth, door, gate' (with article). ⲧⲟⲓⲛⲉⲓ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ is the Lyc. action-noun on ⲉⲓ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'come forth, go out' (cf. ⲧⲟⲓⲛⲃⲱⲗ in glossary). Satan is identified as the threshold through which souls must pass at exit — hence his motivation to set up legal barriers against the Light.

Translated 'the Light who shall slay him.' ⲟⲩⲱⲥϥ̄ = ⲟⲩⲱϣϥ 'shatter, smite, slay' (cf. accumulated ⲟⲩⲱⲥⲡϥ context). The clause continues Satan's quoted edict: he calls the Light by this destructive epithet to inspire fear among the souls.

Translated 'commanded them.' Likely Lyc. form on ⲟⲩⲉϩ-ⲥⲁϩⲛⲉ 'command' or ⲟⲩⲱϩⲉ 'set, place,' with 3pl object suffix. Combined with the following ⲁϩⲧⲣⲟⲩⲣ̄ⲡⲁⲣⲛⲉ 'to make them deny' the verb governs a compulsion-clause.

Translated 'manner' (= ⲥⲙⲟⲧ 'form, fashion'). The Lyc. ⲍⲙⲁⲧ corresponds to Sah. ⲥⲙⲟⲧ; here parallel with line 15 ⲛⲉϩⲍⲙⲁⲧ 'his manners/ways.' Distinct from ⲡⲉⲓⲛⲉ 'likeness' (mandatory consistent translation reserved). 'Manner' captures the fashion/way in which the Light shines.
Translated 'mercies.' Likely Lyc. form for ⲙⲛ̄ⲧⲛⲁⲏⲧ/ⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁ 'mercy, compassion' (cf. accumulated ⲙⲛⲧⲛⲁⲉ 'mercies'). The plural in line 14 (ⲛⲁⲅⲁⲡⲏ 'loves') confirms a positive-affective register.

Translated 'he does seven good things.' ϣⲁϩ- is the Lyc. habitual prefix (= Sah. ϣⲁϥ-) recurring throughout this passage (lines 16, 18, 20, 23, 24, 25-26, 27, 30). ⲥⲁϣϩ = ⲥⲁϣϥ 'seven.' This introduces the structural enumeration of seven goods, of which only the first three survive on this page.

Translated 'while he bears away from them.' Reading ϩ̄ⲃⲓ as the same habitual ϣⲁϩ-ⲃⲓ pattern attested in line 24 ϣⲁϩⲃⲓ ⲍⲱⲱϩ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ⲙ̄ⲙⲁⲩ 'he himself takes away from them.' ⲃⲓ = 'carry, bear, take away.' The line 26 [ⲃ{ⲓ}] ⲡⲕⲉⲕⲉ confirms the pattern: 'he bears the darkness.'

Translated 'draws (them) out.' Reduplicated form on ⲱⲗ 'carry, lift' with directional ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forth.' Habitual ϣⲁϩ- = 'he habitually draws/lifts forth.' The clause forms a typological mirror to lines 24-26 (he bears away fear and darkness).

Translated 'the wakeful ones ... cease their hand.' ⲛⲁⲛⲟⲩⲣ̄ϣⲉ = 'those of vigil/wakefulness' (cf. accumulated ⲛⲓⲁⲛⲟⲩⲣ̄ⲱⲉ 'the Watchers'). ⲕⲁ ⲧⲟⲟⲧ⸗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ = standard Coptic idiom 'leave/cease one's hand from = stop doing.' The night-watchers stand down because the Illuminator's vigilance has replaced theirs.
Translated 'in fear.' ⲍⲟⲩⲣⲉⲧⲉ = Lyc. reflex of ϩⲟⲣⲟⲧⲉ/ϩⲣⲟⲧⲉ 'fear' (cf. ⲑⲣ̄ⲧⲉ in line 24 — same root). The ⲛ̄- is genitive: 'watch of fear' = 'fearful watch.'
